spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **ML pipeline orchestration** models ingestion, data validation, feature engineering, distributed training, evaluation, and model registration as a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)** of idempotent tasks keyed by logical execution date (`ds`) or dataset snapshot.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts URI-Based ML Training DAG (CPU Prep -> Gate -> GPU Train) (DAG Orchestrator -> Spark/Ray CPU -> S3 / Artifact Store -> A100/H100 Pool); Validation Gate -> GPU Train -> Eval -> Registry Promotion (PREP & GATE -> GPU TRAIN -> REGISTERED).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose the orchestrator and task granularity that match your team's lineage and cost profile. Every registered model stores `(git_sha, dataset_snapshot_uri, eval_metrics_json, container_digest)` in the model registry, enabling 1-click reproducible retraining and rollback.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect ML orchestration to Airflow DAGs, feature stores, data quality checks, and GPU serving.

learningJourney.title: What is ML Pipeline Orchestration
learningJourney.explanation:
**ML pipeline orchestration** models ingestion, data validation, feature engineering, distributed training, evaluation, and model registration as a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)** of idempotent tasks keyed by logical execution date (`ds`) or dataset snapshot.

Crucially, the orchestrator acts strictly as the **control plane**—passing lightweight immutable object-storage URIs (`s3://bucket/run_id/features.parquet`) rather than raw DataFrames.

sectionDiagram.summary: Decoupling CPU preprocessing from GPU nodes prevents $2–$4/hr GPUs from sitting idle during SQL/Spark joins.

learningJourney.title: Why cron scripts, XCom DataFrames, and training-serving skew fail
learningJourney.explanation:
Ad-hoc bash/cron pipelines fail silently when upstream schemas drift, waste expensive GPU hours waiting on CPU joins, and cannot reproduce a model from 3 months ago.

Two classic failure modes: **Orchestrator DB Bloat** (serializing DataFrames via Airflow XCom crashes Postgres) and **Training-Serving Skew** (offline Spark/SQL transforms diverge subtly from online Python/Go inference code).

learningJourney.title: Idempotent URI-Passing Task Pattern
learningJourney.explanation: Every task reads an immutable input URI, writes deterministically to a run-scoped output URI, and returns only the URI string.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
# Pass immutable S3 URIs (<4 KB metadata), never raw DataFrames
def validate_and_register(features_uri: str, run_id: str) -> str:
    df = load_parquet_sample(features_uri)
    assert df["label"].isna().mean() < 0.01, "Label null spike detected before GPU allocation"
    manifest_uri = f"s3://ml-artifacts/{run_id}/validated_manifest.json"
    write_json(manifest_uri, {"features_uri": features_uri, "rows": len(df)})
    return manifest_uri
```

benefits: First-class typed artifacts, data-asset lineage graphs, and native K8s GPU pod steps.
costs: Smaller general-purpose ETL operator catalog than Airflow.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why should ML pipeline tasks pass immutable S3/GCS URIs rather than raw DataFrames through the orchestrator's metadata store (e.g., Airflow XCom)?

options.text: S3 automatically trains the model faster
options.feedback: S3 is object storage; the issue is orchestrator database saturation.

options.text: Serializing large DataFrames into the orchestrator's Postgres/MySQL metadata DB saturates it and crashes the scheduler
options.feedback: Correct: keep the orchestrator strictly as a lightweight control plane (<4 KB URI metadata) and store data payloads in object storage.

options.text: Parquet files cannot be read in Python
options.feedback: PyArrow, Pandas, Polars, and Spark all read Parquet natively.
